Summary (FSR‑informed): The FOMC raised the target range for the federal funds rate to 0.75–1.00 percent and will begin balance-sheet runoff on June 1 to address inflation that remains elevated from pandemic-related supply disruptions, the Russia–Ukraine energy shock, and renewed China lockdowns. Consistent with the May 2022 Financial Stability Report, near-term risks are skewed toward higher inflation and weaker activity: higher energy prices and supply bottlenecks are cost-push in nature, and tighter policy transmits through higher borrowing costs and tighter credit, likely weighing on rate-sensitive investment and housing. That said, the FSR also emphasizes that core U.S. financial system resilience is solid—banks have strong capital and liquidity, household delinquencies are low, and direct U.S. exposures to Russia are limited—tempering tail-risk concerns. Net: growth headwinds and gradual disinflation, but with meaningful buffers in the financial system.
